title: I gave Claude Fable 5 one prompt, and it built this end to end.
author: beelllllll
selftext:
I gave Claude (Fable 5) a reference image and a rough prompt to make a Skyrim-style game in Three.js.

It built the game end to end, including melee, magic, enemies, terrain, UI, and Assets using AutoSprite mcp.

A prototype like this used to take forever. Now it was mostly one image, one prompt, and a few follow-ups.

I’m honestly blown away.

All custom assets were made through the [https://www.autosprite.io/](https://www.autosprite.io/) MCP feature. (Full disclosure: I’m the founder of AutoSprite.)

**Prompt:**

>

From there I fixed a bug where the rocks were too small and the enemy slime was going through me.

I’m genuinely excited for what’s coming. Things are moving so fast, and it feels like a golden era for game developers (and the world in general).

comments.author: beelllllll
comments.body:
I'm not sure why the actual prompt section got erased, but here it is:

  
Build a complete Three.js + Vite game inspired by Skyrim, matching this reference image. Use AutoSprite MCP for enemies and 3D assets, procedural terrain, and AutoSprite image and 3d generation for UI and weapons. Make it playable end to end with melee and magic combat.

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body:
Yup that is basically the final shortcoming with these models that really separates from the rest is getting good 2d / 3d assets. So I have it plug into AutoSprite MCP (mcp is a tool that allows your coding agent to talk to other apps) 

Other examples are blender mcp or unity mcp
